author: reek
body: The calendar, moved out of `apps/guios/CalendarApp.codex` when the guios shell retired into GopDesk. The date arithmetic is that chapter's, unchanged.

author: reek
body: What changed is the rendering. The old one laid out a two-row header as widgets and then placed all 28 to 31 day numbers itself with hand-computed pixel positions into a GopBuf. Here the whole month is a widget tree: six rows of seven cells, laid out by the same flex engine as everything else, so the grid divides the pane's real width instead of a `(win-w - 32) / 7` the caller had to get right.

author: reek
body: **Today is a button and every other day is a label.** That is the whole highlight mechanism, and it is deliberate: a button paints its background from the theme and a label does not, so the current day stands out using only the two widget kinds `GopComposite` already draws. The old chapter filled a rectangle behind the number itself, which is a thing a pane cannot do when it hands back a tree rather than a buffer.

author: reek
body: This chapter reads no clock. The RTC is a port device and reading it is an effect; GopDesk already owns `rtc-read` and passes the date in, so the tree stays pure and the same three numbers can be handed in by a test.

author: reek
body: Day of week for 1 January, counting from Sunday = 0. The + 1 is the anchor: 1 January year 1 was a Monday in the proleptic calendar.

author: reek
body: A cell is addressed by its position in the six-by-seven grid, and the day it carries is `pos - dow1 + 1`. Positions before the first of the month and past the last carry a blank label rather than being absent, so every row has seven children and the columns line up under the weekday header.

author: reek
body: Six rows always. A month can start on a Saturday and run 31 days, which needs 6 rows; drawing only the rows a given month fills would make the pane change height from month to month.
